title: I'll play your mobile game on stream
author: Dramatic-Mongoose-95
selftext:
Hey all,

Two question:

(1) did you make a Mobile (or mobile web friendly) game?  
(2) do you want to watch me play it on my twitch stream?

If you answered YES and YES, please drop a link below, and I'll respond later with a link to the stream after I've played it.

I need to do another round of testing in my streaming app, and doing this event makes it fun for me, because testing is boring AF.

If I have broken your rules, please delete this post and accept my apologies 

Thank you

replies.author: nvrcr
replies.body:
Super appreciate the playthrough and review, and I gave you a follow. To answer your Qs: 

* No assets were made with AI. They're just simple vector art so I drew/animated them myself. AI was used primarily for feature development, bug fixing, and balance tuning.
* Ads: They're not bringing much money cause they're just banner ads -- a few cents really at my volume. I didn't put any video ads because I found them highly intrusive. I can see how the banner could be distracting (especially depending on content).

replies.author: SaintFX
replies.body:
This was great to watch - thank you for checking it out and the kind review! This helped me spot some things I could make better.

\- You’re right about the symbols - those simply indicate the category for a word.  
\- Near the top you’ll see requests for words of a certain category. If you can’t think of one, tap the request text and it’ll give you a clue to a word you haven’t used before. Bonus bytes if you don’t need a clue  
\- Below that you’ll sometimes get a clue for related words. You can also tap that text to see the clue for it. Like “MOM and H\_G” - the word would be HUG.  
\- Words get more expensive to compile the more programs you have. So killing the programs that aren’t as big of a byte generator, or programs that scramble others, helps to make the next compile cheaper (I need to explain this better)

I know the tooltips can get annoying so I was trying to not pop a bunch all at once and introduce new concepts as you encounter them. Thanks again for checking it out!
